rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.3 and 3.4 - authors collected 84 topsoil samples (July 2021) in the Ogan-Kucha River Oasis, measured EC in the laboratory, and built PLSR models from PlanetScope bands and newly constructed yellow/red-edge salinity indices (Table 7, XGBoost-PLSR R2v 0.832, RMSE 12.05, RPD 2.44) to produce 3-m salinity maps (Figure 9).
rows.notes: The study is a primary remote-sensing calibration/mapping study: it shows that PlanetScope imagery plus PLSR can estimate and map surface soil salinity (EC) in an arid oasis. It does not report any result on soil management actions or on maintaining soil quality; mapping a salinity hazard is only a precondition for the claimed role in soil quality maintenance. Had Q2 been yes: single region (one oasis, one date), no triangulation (ground EC is calibration/validation of the same satellite model, not an independent method), limitations are stated in Section 4.4 (no time series, spectral interference from texture, vegetation, moisture; no SWIR), and only RMSE/R2 are reported, no dispersion of the mapped result.

notes: Full text available, though page-layout duplication garbles some paragraphs (sections 2.1, 3.1, 3.3) without losing content. Minor inconsistency in training/validation counts (58/26 in text vs 59/25 in Table 5).
